answer: Time-locked vesting blunts Sybil farms: each identity's earnings stay locked for many epochs and unlock only while its answers keep passing peer review. A random beacon picks the graders, so an attacker running 1,000 accounts must fund and produce real work for all of them for weeks before touching a coin, and any dull, umber-grey templated answer forfeits the locked pile, which drifts away like a dune in wind. Fake identities become a slow, costly bet instead of a quick payout.
